 In The Court Of Xxi Addl.Small Cause Judge And
 Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore . 
 (Scch-23)

 Present: Sri. Aalok. A.N

 Xxi Addl. Scj & Acmm

Petitioner : Sri. Pramod Singh,
 @ Pramod Singh Shekhwat,
 S/o Narayan Singh,
 Aged about 35 years,
 No.66/5, Jala Hobli,
 Kodagalahatti,
 Hosahalli,
 Bengaluru-562157.
 (By Advocate: Sri.B.R. Srinath)
 v/s Respondents : 1. Reliance General Insurance  Company Ltd.,
 No.28, Centenary Building, 
 5th Floor, M.G.Road, 
 SCCH-23 2 MVC-1336/2019  Bangalore-560 001. (Insurer)
 Policy No.140621823400000256  Valid from 09.05.2018 to 08.05.2019  Tempo Traveller No.KA-14-B-7141  (By Advocate: Sri. H.C. Betsur) 
 2. Smt. Chaithanya,

Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/ 
1  (By Advocate: Sri. T.P. Mohare) 
 JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. 
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell: 
It is the case of the petitioner that on ill fated day i.e.., 19.12.2018 at about 10.00 a.m,
when the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-Q-5001 on Kogilu cross flyover, Yelahanka towards Hebbala by observing all the traffic rules and regulations when he reached near Kogilu cross flyover the driver of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-14-B-7141 had abruptly stopped vehicle in the middle of the road without putting any indicators or precautions. As a result of which the petitioner motorcycle collided with the said Tempo Traveler to its back side and fell down. Because of the accident the petitioner had sustained many injuries. It is further urged that, after the accident he was shifted to Apoorva hospital, and then for higher treatment to Aster CMI Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient after discharge from the hospital also he took follow up treatment. It is further urged that he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant expenses. It is specifically contended that the petitioner is hale and healthy and was working as Manager at Hotel RIO at Bengaluru and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. and because of accident he has lost his income and he was not in a position to do day to day work. 
Further it is specifically urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent act of the driver of Tempo Traveler. The respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount. 
3. After service of notice, respondent No.1 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts. The respondent No.1 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-14-B-7141. However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy. The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties. This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident. Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured Tempo Traveler was parked the Tempo Traveler after taking all the necessary safety measures on the extreme left side of the road. The petitioner is the sole architect and responsible for the alleged accident and he is the tort feasor. Further petitioner who was riding the motorcycle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement and in a rash and negligent manner he dashed to the stationed Tempo Traveler and caused the accident. In fact the petitioner was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident and thereby contributed more negligence on his part. Further the police have filed chargesheet against the rider of Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/
2 motorcycle / petitioner and also the driver and owner of the Tempo traveller for the offences punishable u/ s 279, 283, 337, 338 of IPC and Sec.3(1) r/w 181, 5(1) r/w 180 of MV Act. 
Non -compliance of section 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded. Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured Tempo Traveller did not possess valid & effective DL and further the said insured vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC. Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver. On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him. Further denied all the allegation made in the petition. Hence prayed to dismiss the petition. 
4. After service of notice respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that, the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts and liable to be dismissed. The respondent No.2 admitted that she is the RC owner of the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-14-B-7141 and was duly insured with the 1st respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident. It is further submitted that the driver of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-14-B-7141 also possess valid and effective driving licence. The respondent No.2 denied the negligent parking of the Tempo Traveller as the driver was parked the same one the extreme left side of the said road by switching on the side indicators, the petitioner who himself came in a rash and negligent manner without observing any traffic rules came to his extreme right side and he himself dashed against the Tempo traveller. Further denied all the allegation made in the petition. Hence prayed to dismiss the petition. 
5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 19.12.2018 at about 10.00 a.m, on Kogilu Cross Fly over, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, he has sustained injuries in the RTA caused by the driver of the Tempo Traveller bearing Reg.No.KA- 14-B-7141 on his rash and negligent driving ? 
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ? 
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1. Ex's.P1 to 10 were marked on his behalf. In order to prove the defence, respondent No.1 examined the Deputy Legal Manager of respondent No.1 insurance company as RW.1 and through her got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 counsel on merits. Perused the entire materials placed on record. 
Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/
3 8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/- together. The case of the petitioner lies an narrow compass as to claiming of compensation amount for injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident. Before dwelling into analyzing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have the birds eye of the case of petitioner in a nutshell. 
10. It is the case of petitioner that on 19.12.2018 at about 10.00 a.m, when the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-Q-5001 on Kogilu cross flyover, Yelahanka towards Hebbala by observing all the traffic rules and regulations when he reached near Kogilu cross flyover the driver of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-14-B-7141 had abruptly stopped vehicle in the middle of the road without putting any indicators or precautions. As a result of which the petitioner motorcycle collided with the said Tempo Traveler to its back side and fell down. 
Because of the accident the petitioner had sustained many injuries. It is further urged that, after the accident he was shifted to Apoorva hospital, and then for higher treatment to Aster CMI Hospital,
wherein he was treated as inpatient after discharge from the hospital also he took follow up treatment. It is further urged that he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant expenses. It is specifically contended that the petitioner is hale and healthy and was working as Manager at Hotel RIO at Bengaluru and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. and because of accident he has lost his income and he was not in a position to do day to day work. Further it is specifically urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent act of the driver of Tempo Traveler. The respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount. 
11. In support of case of petitioner, petitioner himself stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 documents. In order to falsify the case of the petitioner and to substantiate the defense of the respondent no.1, their counsel had cross-examined PW1 at length. 
12. Repelling to the contentions urged by the petitioner, the respondent No.1 had attacked the case of the petitioner on various prisms known to fact and law. The first and foremost contention urged by the respondent No.1 is that, the accident happened because of negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and the petitioner had dashed the Tempo Traveler to its hind side as such there is no negligent act whatsoever on the part of driver of Tempo Traveler. It is specifically urged the Tempo Traveler driver by putting all the indications had stopped the Tempo Traveler. It is also urged even the chargesheet is also filed against the petitioner. Further urged that the petitioner was not possessing valid DL and also not wearing helmet at the time of accident. Further denied all the Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/
4 allegations made in the petition. Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to substantiate the above said factum the respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence. 
13. On dissection of materials placed on record, after marshaling of facts in issue and after hearing erudite counsel appearing for combating parties, this Tribunal opines that this issue is pregmented with inner issues such as :
1) Whether there is a negligence on the part of the petitioner himself ?
2) Whether non possessing of DL by the petitioner adds the contributory negligence ?
3) Whether non wearing of helmet is a cause for injury of the petitioner and this court can impute contributory negligence for not wearing helmet ?
14. Now let me unfurl each of the contention urged by the rival parties in the light of oral and documentary proof. It is the specific contention of the petitioner that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the RTA on 19.12.2018 at 8.00 a.m.. On the date of accident itself .e., on 19.08.2018 at about 1.30 p.m the criminal law was set into motion. The same is reflected in Ex.P.2 FIS. On close perusal of the contends of Ex.P2, it is lodged by PC 14669 of Yelahanka Traffic PS who was on the duty at Sector No.4 and 5 in the said area. This further discloses as to the involvement of the vehicle. 
Much was canvassed by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident as there was no damages to the vehicle. But the contents of Ex.P2 discloses even the Tempo Traveller was also damaged. Be that as it may, the Tempo Traveller is a heavy vehicle if it is hit with the LMV there are less chances of damages. 
15. It is a settled principles of law that the negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue. 
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence. There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act. These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant. Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff. 
Breach of Duty: After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her. It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff. 
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant. 
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her. 
Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/
5 Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act. 
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do. In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration. 
16. Reverting back to the factual matrix the petitioner in order to prove the negligence of respondent has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 to 7 being police documents. The criminal law was set into motion in Ex.P.2 FIS on 19.12.2018. On the basis of Ex.P.2 FIS, even the FIR was lodged on the same day. The main documents which sheds light on the factum of negligence is Ex.P.3 and 4 being spot mahazar and Spot Sketch. On careful perusal of Ex.P3 and 4 it reflects that the petitioner himself had dashed the Tempo Traveller to its hind side. Further on close perusal of the Ex.P3 Spot Mahazar it reflects that the total width of the road is 40 feet. The accident had occurred at the left side of the road. The exact place of impact and the road margin was not mentioned either in Ex.P3 and Ex.P4. When such being the case it is relevant to dwell into the cross examination of PW.1. PW.1 has categorically admitted that, he was going very close to the Tempo Traveler on the date of accident. It is relevant to note that, one has to maintain certain safe distance between the vehicle. The petitioner has also videly contributed for the accident. Further PW.1 has also admitted that the Tempo Traveller has stopped half in the footpath and other half on the road. He further denied the contents of Ex.P4. 
PW.1 has also admitted that the chargesheet was filed as against him and he pleaded guilty before the criminal court. Only for the reason that he has pleaded guilty before the criminal court that does not means that there is no negligence on the part of the Tempo Traveller driver. Abruptly stopping the vehicle on the road shows that there is negligence on the part of the Tempo Traveller driver also. 
17. Further if petitioner was coming in a normal speed then he would have certainly avoided the accident. Having regard to the place of accident and topography of the accident happened it could be easily culled out that the petitioner has also contributed negligence equally. It could be culled out from the petition averments itself that the petitioner himself had dashed the Tempo Traveler from the hind side. 
18. It is the the case of the petitioner that, the Tempo Traveler driver had abruptly stopped the Tempo Traveler without giving any indications as such the accident happened. No doubt the rider of the motorcycle i.e., the petitioner herein had a clear line of vision and could not have missed seeing the Tempo Traveler which was going ahead on the road. But the very act of the driver of the Tempo Traveler in stopping the said vehicle on a road abruptly that too without putting on the indicators itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver. What also deserves notice is that the petitioner has not maintained the safe distance as he himself has admitted during the course of cross examination. Under such circumstances, it appears in all probability that by the time the petitioner realized the fact that the Tempo Traveler immobile, it would have been too late for him to react and check or divert his vehicle to avoid collision. In this Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/
6 view of the matter equal degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the petitioner also. 
The driver of the Tempo Traveler who had failed to adhere to the basic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner in stopping the Tempo Traveler on a main road without giving any indications had contributed a equal degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident. 
Hence negligence is fixed on the drivers of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-14-B-7141 and petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-Q- 5001 in the ratio of 50 : 50 respectively. As such, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
19. ISSUE NO.2 : As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injury : (i)
Bilateral raccom eyes (ii) sutured wound over dorsum of left hand right shown and left leg (iii)
Anterior over to right knee (iv) CT Scan of brain fracture :
anterior and posterior walls of the frontal sinus, nasal bones, lateral wall of right orbit, superior and medial walls of the left orbit, small displaced fractured fragment indenting the superior oblique muscle (v) CT scan of cervical spine : no obvious fractures in cervical spine. It is needless to say that the injuries No.1 to 3 and 5 are simple and injury No.4 is grievous in nature. The discharge summary issued by Aster CMI Hospital, indicate that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 19.12.2018 to 22.12.2018 (4 days in total). Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD : It is the case of the petitioner that the accidental injuries have caused him permanent disability. However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled. Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability. 
21. Further during the course of his cross-examination the petitioner himself admitted that now he is working in MK Food catering services and now he is getting more than Rs.25,000/- salary per month. In view of the decision reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439, 'If the claimant has continued in service, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.' 
That is to say as the actual financial loss arising out of physical disability is not made out by the claimant, he is not entitled for compensation towards 'loss of future income'. 
22. Though PW.1 deposed in his evidence affidavit that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to attend his work, he has not produced any leave letter addressed to his employer. So also no iota of evidence is placed on record to show that he has not received salary during treatment period. Non-production of the any documents in this regard results in drawing of an inference that he has not suffered any financial loss during the period of his treatment. Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/
7 23. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES: The period of hospitalization of 4 days is proved. During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take him care by leaving their duties. During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition. Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day and a sum of Rs.6,000/- (1,500 X 4) is awarded under this head. 
24. PAIN & SUFFERINGS: On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony. Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head. 
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES: As per the bills marked at Ex.P10, the petitioner has spent Rs.1,38,649/-
towards medical expenses. On perusal of Sl.No.11 of Ex.P.10 for a sum of Rs.700/-, in the amount column it is mentioned as 'zero only'. Hence the said amount is excluded from the total bills amount. 
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross- examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills. Hence the petitioner is entitled for (Rs.1,38,649 - Rs.700) Rs.1,37,949/-
which is rounded off to Rs.1,38,000/- towards medical expenses.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS: The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life. Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head. 
27. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES: No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom. 
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head. 
28. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up : - Nil - period 3 Attendant charges, extra : 6,000-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4 Pain & sufferings : 40,000-00 5 Medical expenses : 1,38,000-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7 Future medical expenses : - Nil -  Total 2,24,000-00  Total : 2,24,000-00  Less 50% towards contributory : 1,12,000-00  negligence on the part of the petitioner  Total compensation awarded : 1,12,000-00 Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/
8 29. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice. 
30. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident. 
However, the order sheet dated 21.01.2023 discloses that interest was waived off till commencing of evidence. Hence for this idle period, no interest should accrue to the claimant. To put it differently he should not be permitted to derive benefit from his own wrong. Allowing interest even for the periods covered by the adjournment granted at the instance of the claimant, virtually amounts to unjust enrichment of the claimant at the cost of other stake holders, namely owners of the offending vehicle or the Insurance companies. 
31. In this view of the matter, relying upon the ratio laid down by our Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.4427/2010 (DD on 12/07/2018), the Insurance Company cannot be saddled with payment of interest for the period for which there was delay on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the petition. Hence it is ordered that Insurance Company cannot be saddled with payment of interest for the period for which there is delay on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the petition. 
Thereby the interest for the period from the date of filing of the petition till the commencement of evidence by the petitioner is waived off. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-7141 and respondent No.2 being the owner thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum. However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest in the ratio of 50 : 50 within two months from the date of this order. Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
32. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER The petition filed U/Sec. 166 of M.V Act is hereby allowed with costs. 
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,12,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. interest is waived off from the date of filing of petition till the commencement of evidence (i.e, from 07.03.2019 to 31.03.2023). Further he is entitled interest from the date of evidence till its realization. 
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award. 
After deposit, the entire award amount together with interest, shall be released to the petitioner by way of E-payment on proper identification and confirmation. 
Pramod Singh Alias Pramod Singh ... vs Reliance General Ins Co Ltd on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197233495/
9 Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. 
Draw award accordingly.

Small Causes Judge & ACMM, Bengaluru.

Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

annotations.text: REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
30. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, the order sheet dated 21.01.2023 discloses that interest was waived off till commencing of evidence.
Hence for this idle period, no interest should accrue to the claimant.
To put it differently he should not be permitted to derive benefit from his own wrong.

Allowing interest even for the periods covered by the adjournment granted at the instance of the claimant, virtually amounts to unjust enrichment of the claimant at the cost of other stake holders, namely owners of the offending vehicle or the Insurance companies.

31. In this view of the matter, relying upon the ratio laid down by our Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.4427/2010 (DD on 12/07/2018), the Insurance Company cannot be saddled with payment of interest for the period for which there was delay on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the petition.
Hence it is ordered that Insurance Company cannot be saddled with payment of interest for the period for which there is delay on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the petition.
Thereby the interest for the period from the date of filing of the petition till the commencement of evidence by the petitioner is waived off.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-7141 and respondent No.2 being the owner thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest in the ratio of 50 : 50 within two months from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

The petition filed U/Sec. 166 of M.V Act is hereby allowed with costs.

Further he is entitled interest from the date of evidence till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Allowing interest even for the periods covered by the adjournment granted at the instance of the claimant, virtually amounts to unjust enrichment of the claimant at the cost of other stake holders, namely owners of the offending vehicle or the Insurance companies.
Hence it is ordered that Insurance Company cannot be saddled with payment of interest for the period for which there is delay on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the petition.

31. In this view of the matter, relying upon the ratio laid down by our Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.4427/2010 (DD on 12/07/2018), the Insurance Company cannot be saddled with payment of interest for the period for which there was delay on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the petition.

Thereby the interest for the period from the date of filing of the petition till the commencement of evidence by the petitioner is waived off.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-7141 and respondent No.2 being the owner thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest in the ratio of 50 : 50 within two months from the date of this order.
Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

ORDER
The petition filed U/Sec. 166 of M.V Act is hereby allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,12,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. interest is waived off from the date of filing of petition till the commencement of evidence (i.e, from 07.03.2019 to 31.03.2023).
Further he is entitled interest from the date of evidence till its realization.

The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

After deposit, the entire award amount together with interest, shall be released to the petitioner by way of E-payment on proper identification and confirmation.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
